title: dedicated-autoscaler: smoother burst controls and utilization reporting improvements
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: fleets observed occasional token-burst storms after transient traffic spikes which cause short-term request queueing and uneven utilization reporting. This PR smooths the Dedicated autoscaler's tokenbucket burst control and improves telemetry so operators can reliably track burst consumption and queued request counts. The goals are: 1) reduce transient queueing during short spikes without impacting long-tail throughput guarantees, 2) make burst consumption visible in metrics and dashboards, and 3) expose safe admin controls for burst windows. Changes include a tunable smoothing window for the tokenbucket, a bounded backlog queue policy to avoid unbounded memory growth, additional Prometheus metrics for burst_tokens_used and burst_queue_length, admin API surface for burst_config, an update to the autoscaler simulation harness for regression tests, and docs + release notes. Checklist: [x] tokenbucket smoothing algorithm implemented and unit tested, [x] bounded backlog queue policy implemented, [x] telemetry added (metrics, tags), [x] admin API and console wiring, [x] integration tests in perf-canary, [x] docs updated, [x] rollout plan with gradual traffic ramp and monitoring. Rollout plan: deploy to canary Dedicated fleet (10%) with conservative smoothing defaults, monitor burst_queue_length and p99 latency for 24h, increment to 50% if stable, then full rollout. Observability: added metrics are prefixed dedicated_autoscaler_ and instrumented with cluster_id and fleet_id tags; dashboards updated in observability-pack. Related work: ENG-3421 (burst policy improvements), ENG-3502 (utilization reporting), SUP-1182 incident follow-up. Migration/compatibility notes: new admin API is additive; default smoothing values preserve prior behavior if unset.
commits: Refactor tokenbucket smoothing algorithm (introduce exponential moving average window)
Implement bounded backlog queue, add hard caps and soft-fallbacks to token consumption
Expose admin API and console settings for burst_config (proto + UI wiring)
Add unit and integration tests, update perf-canary scenarios
Docs: docs/dedicated/autoscaler.md release notes and runbook updates

release_notes: Improved Dedicated autoscaler burst handling: introduces tokenbucket smoothing to reduce transient queueing, bounded backlog queue policy to avoid unbounded memory growth, new metrics (dedicated_autoscaler_burst_tokens_used, dedicated_autoscaler_burst_queue_length) for better utilization reporting, and admin controls for burst windows. Safe rollout planned via canary.
additional_context: CI: initial run had one flaky unit test (TestAutoscalerStartStop) failing due to race in test harness; rerun succeeded. Performance: internal perf-canary run shows 18-22% reduction in short-term p99 latency spikes during synthetic bursts and no measurable impact to sustained throughput. Ops: dashboards updated and alert thresholds recommended in observability-pack. Admins can adjust smoothing window and max_burst_tokens on a per-fleet basis.
notes_for_oncall: If increased queue length is observed post-deploy, reduce smoothing window or lower max_burst_tokens; emergency rollback path: feature flag 'smoothing_enabled' per fleet to revert to prior tokenbucket behavior without code rollback.
compatibility: Additive API changes only; default behavior unchanged if new fields are omitted.
risk_assessment: Low-medium: algorithmic change to token consumption. Covered by unit tests, canary rollout, and per-fleet disable flag. Monitoring and runbook updated.
